grades.quote: sleep() releases the condition lock so that the code calling wakeup() can proceed. sleep() also context-switches to the scheduler in order to let other threads run while it is waiting. The implementation performs these two steps in a way that is atomic (indivisible) with respect to wakeup(), to prevent lost wake-ups.
grades.reason: Directly explains that the condition lock must be held and passed to sleep, so wakeup cannot run between the condition check and sleep. It also says sleep releases the lock and context-switches atomically with respect to wakeup, which prevents a lost wake-up.
This is a list of exercises. It does not explain how sleep releases the lock without losing a wakeup. Exercise 2 only asks whether the lock argument could be dropped.
